headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: open-webui’s persistent, tool-rich sessions can ingest gpt-researcher outputs and sensitive files by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, browse, and call MCP; open-webui supports MCP, plugins, and tool calling. That creates a plausible bridge where content from A can be fed into B as instructions. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem or clipboard, so this is not high, but the interaction exists in default tool-enabled setups.
conditions: IF open-webui is configured with MCP or tool connectors that ingest gpt-researcher outputs
IF gpt-researcher writes research text into a file or artifact that open-webui reads
mitigations: Disable MCP/tool connectors between the two agents
Require provenance tags on all imported content
Route A’s outputs through a human review step before B reads them
Use separate workspaces or volumes for each agent
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher handles API keys and local documents, while open-webui touches persistent memory, files, and API keys and can use mounted volumes plus external APIs. In a shared workspace or mounted volume, A’s sensitive research artifacts can flow into B’s persistent context and outbound requests. The default tool-rich setup makes leakage plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory or mounted volume
IF open-webui indexes or uploads files from that shared location
IF gpt-researcher stores API-key-bearing prompts or research notes in files
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Remove secrets from any shared workspace immediately
Disable file ingestion in open-webui for the shared path
Use least-privilege API keys for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and subprocess execution, and both support multiple instances. open-webui also advertises Redis-backed shared sessions, so concurrent writes to shared mutable state are plausible. gpt-researcher’s planner/execution/publisher model adds another writer path. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, database, or git repository
IF open-webui is deployed with Redis-backed shared sessions across workers
IF gpt-researcher publisher and open-webui tools mutate the same resource concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Avoid shared git branches or shared DB rows
Run one agent at a time for mutable tasks
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control to shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher system that produces research outputs, and open-webui can consume documents, notes, and tool outputs in persistent sessions. If B treats A’s research as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or persisted memory. The profiles show no built-in verification barrier, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF open-webui imports gpt-researcher reports into chat or memory without verification
IF B uses A’s citations or facts to generate user-facing actions or documents
IF A’s outputs are forwarded into B’s tool calls
mitigations: Require a verification checklist before import
Mark A’s outputs as untrusted by default
Keep A’s outputs read-only in B
Add a second-pass fact checker before any action
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating for downstream tool use

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle files and API keys, but open-webui additionally stores persistent memory, analytics, and model-evaluation data, while gpt-researcher handles research queries, reports, and local documents. That creates a realistic retention-policy mismatch on the same data class if they share content. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so medium fits best.
conditions: IF the same user data is stored in both agents
IF open-webui retains prompts or artifacts longer than gpt-researcher retains reports
IF regulated data is placed into either agent’s persistent memory or analytics
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared sessions
Set short retention windows for both systems
Disable analytics on sensitive deployments
Document which data classes each agent may store
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems
